source_refs.note: Exercise 10.2 Q10 (i)-(ii), book p.190 (PDF 195). Key PDF 308: (i) 33/65, -56/65 matches; (ii) 416/425, 3/5 wrong (correct -304/425, 297/425). Sympy; solution book PDF 919-922 agrees.

blocks.prompt: 10 (i) Find \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) and \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\), given that \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{3}{4}\), \(\cos\beta = \dfrac{5}{13}\) and neither the terminal side of the angle of measure \(\alpha\) nor that of \(\beta\) is in the quadrant I.
blocks.explanation:
We are not told the quadrants directly; we must work them out from the signs and the condition "not in quadrant I".
Then find all four ratios and use the sum formulas.
Plan: quadrant of \(\alpha\), quadrant of \(\beta\), missing ratios, formulas.
steps:
Given: \(\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}\), \(\cos\beta = \frac{5}{13}\); neither angle in quadrant I.
To find: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) and \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\).
Method: Decide the quadrants, find \(\sin\alpha, \cos\alpha, \sin\beta\) with the right signs, then
\[\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]

Quadrants
\[\tan\alpha > 0 \Rightarrow \text{I or III} \Rightarrow \alpha \in \text{III}\]
\[\cos\beta > 0 \Rightarrow \text{I or IV} \Rightarrow \beta \in \text{IV}\]
Why: Quadrant I is excluded by the question.

Ratios of \(\alpha\) (quadrant III)
\[\sec^2\alpha = 1 + \dfrac{9}{16} = \dfrac{25}{16}\]
\[\cos\alpha = -\dfrac{4}{5},\quad \sin\alpha = \tan\alpha\cos\alpha = -\dfrac{3}{5}\]
Why: \(1 + \tan^2 = \sec^2\); in quadrant III sine and cosine are negative.

Ratio of \(\beta\) (quadrant IV)
\[\sin\beta = -\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{25}{169}} = -\dfrac{12}{13}\]
Why: In quadrant IV sine is negative.

Find \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\)
\[= \left(-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\dfrac{5}{13} + \left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right)\left(-\dfrac{12}{13}\right)\]
\[= -\dfrac{15}{65} + \dfrac{48}{65} = \dfrac{33}{65}\]
Why: Sine of a sum; denominator \(5 \times 13 = 65\).

Find \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\)
\[= \left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right)\dfrac{5}{13} - \left(-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\left(-\dfrac{12}{13}\right)\]
\[= -\dfrac{20}{65} - \dfrac{36}{65} = -\dfrac{56}{65}\]
Why: The second product is \(+\frac{36}{65}\) and is subtracted.

Check
\[33^2 + 56^2 = 1089 + 3136 = 4225 = 65^2 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1\) for the angle \(\alpha + \beta\); the key also gives \(\frac{33}{65}, -\frac{56}{65}\).

blocks.prompt: 10 (ii) Find \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) and \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\), given that \(\tan\alpha = -\dfrac{15}{8}\) and \(\sin\beta = -\dfrac{7}{25}\) and neither the terminal side of the angle of measure \(\alpha\) nor that of \(\beta\) is in the quadrant IV.
blocks.explanation:
Again the quadrants must be deduced from the signs and the condition "not in quadrant IV".
Then complete the ratios and use the sum formulas.
Plan: quadrants, missing ratios, formulas, check.
steps:
Given: \(\tan\alpha = -\frac{15}{8}\), \(\sin\beta = -\frac{7}{25}\); neither angle in quadrant IV.
To find: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) and \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\).
Method: quadrants, then \(\sin\alpha, \cos\alpha, \cos\beta\), then the sum formulas.

Quadrants
\[\tan\alpha < 0 \Rightarrow \text{II or IV} \Rightarrow \alpha \in \text{II}\]
\[\sin\beta < 0 \Rightarrow \text{III or IV} \Rightarrow \beta \in \text{III}\]
Why: Quadrant IV is excluded by the question.

Ratios of \(\alpha\) (quadrant II)
\[\sec^2\alpha = 1 + \dfrac{225}{64} = \dfrac{289}{64}\]
\[\cos\alpha = -\dfrac{8}{17},\quad \sin\alpha = \tan\alpha\cos\alpha = \dfrac{15}{17}\]
Why: In quadrant II cosine is negative and sine positive.

Ratio of \(\beta\) (quadrant III)
\[\cos\beta = -\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{49}{625}} = -\dfrac{24}{25}\]
Why: In quadrant III cosine is negative.

Find \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\)
\[= \left(-\dfrac{8}{17}\right)\left(-\dfrac{24}{25}\right) - \dfrac{15}{17}\left(-\dfrac{7}{25}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{192}{425} + \dfrac{105}{425} = \dfrac{297}{425}\]
Why: Minus a negative product becomes plus.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: For part (ii) the answer key prints \(\frac{416}{425}\) and \(\frac{3}{5}\). These cannot be the sine and cosine of one angle, since \(\left(\frac{416}{425}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2 \ne 1\), and they do not follow from the printed data. The correct values are \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = -\frac{304}{425}\), \(\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \frac{297}{425}\).
